HEAVY WORK-CLASS / 3,000 M

R-4000 Heavy Work-Class ROV

Power and payload for deep-water engineering.

A 3.3 t heavy work-class ROV rated to 3,000 m with a 200 kg payload and titanium-alloy frame, for deep-water engineering maintenance and resource exploration.

Read the application guide

Configuration checks

  • Match the 3,000 m rating to the project depth with margin; a 6,000 m version is custom work.
  • Confirm the vessel, launch and recovery system, umbilical and power supply for a 3.3 t vehicle.
  • Specify manipulators, tools and survey sensors, and the crew and training plan.

COMPLETE SYSTEM

Specify more than
the vehicle.

The manufacturer describes a titanium-alloy frame, composite pressure-resistant buoyancy and a high-power electric drive. A 3,000 m rating is not full ocean depth, and the 6,000 m option is offered as custom development rather than an existing delivery. Heavy systems are quoted per project.

Confirm in the delivered scope

  • Vehicle, tether management system (TMS) and umbilical
  • Launch and recovery system or A-frame interface
  • Control container, shore power and software
  • Manipulators, tools and survey sensors
  • Spares, manuals, commissioning and crew training

Standard, optional and custom items must be listed separately in the quotation.

QUESTIONS

Before you specify the R-4000.

Can the R-4000 work at 6,000 m?

The standard rating is 3,000 m. The manufacturer offers a 6,000 m version as a custom option; depth, components and testing would be defined for that project.

How does it compare with the R-2000?

The R-4000 is rated three times deeper (3,000 m vs 1,000 m) and carries twice the payload (200 kg vs 100 kg), but weighs 3.3 t against 2.2 t and needs a larger launch system.
